fr.elements: Main Building; Secondary Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Access Road; Dumpster Enclosure
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Mark each access point with a visible address or unit identifier so responders can confirm entry location on arrival.

• Post the building address or property identifier at the primary access road entry so it is visible from the street.

• Mark the secondary building with its own unit or building identifier to distinguish it from the main building during a response.

• Trim vegetation along the internal drive aisle where dense growth reduces visibility or narrows the travel path for emergency vehicles.

• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles and obstructions to allow emergency vehicles to reach both structures.

• Mark the rear access route with directional signage identifying which building or area it serves.

• Keep the rear access route clear of stored materials, equipment, or vehicles that would block emergency vehicle movement.

• Keep the dumpster enclosure positioned so it does not block vehicle movement along the drive aisle or access to either building.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Large Paved Area; Building Cluster; Vegetation Near Building; Limited Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or thin vegetation growing directly against or within a few feet of the buildings in the cluster where limited separation is visible.
• Trim tree branches that extend over or close to any building rooflines within the tree clusters near the building cluster.
• Keep the large paved area clear of any dead leaves, debris, or plant material that may accumulate along its edges.
• Thin the scattered trees and shrubs in areas where vegetation connects closely to the building cluster without a clear open gap.
• Maintain open movement corridors around all buildings so that access from multiple directions remains unobstructed.
• Keep all access routes clear of encroaching vegetation along their edges so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
